source: Year offsets from stablebound-india docs/RUNNING.md: 'Kharif, Autumn and Winter are sown and harvested within the first calendar year' and 'year is the harvest year'. Months are the standard Indian sowing/harvest window.
RUNNING.md: 'Rabi and Summer are sown in the first and harvested in the second'; year is the harvest year, so sowing falls in the previous calendar year.

UNRESOLVED - see docs/SEASONS.md. RUNNING.md groups Summer with Rabi as sown-in-first/harvested-in-second, which would make planting_year_offset -1. But the zaid season runs March-June, which is the SECOND calendar year of a July-June agricultural year, giving 0. Recorded as 0 on the agronomy; needs Michael's call.
RUNNING.md: sown and harvested within the first calendar year. Autumn is aus rice.
RUNNING.md: sown and harvested within the first calendar year. Winter is aman rice, harvested Nov-Dec of the same year.

RUNNING.md: 'Whole Year rows carry the first calendar year of their agricultural year, which is a sowing-year label rather than a harvest-year one', and for the crops always filed this way the harvest falls mostly in the following calendar year. So year is NOT the harvest year here. The +1 holds for the perennials (coconut, black pepper, cassava, banana, arecanut, cashew, garlic) and sugarcane; for the mixed-season crops (onion, potato, ginger, chillies, tobacco, sweet potato, sesame) it is crop-dependent. No single month applies.
DERIVED from the source's Start/End Period on 1,908 rows: start month 3, end month 8, both in the same calendar year as `Year` (offset 0 on every row).
DERIVED from the source's Start/End Period on 1,961 rows: start month 3, end month 11, offset 0 on every row. The March start covers the seedbed; transplanting is later.

DERIVED from the source's Start/End Period on 1,969 rows: start month 11 in the PREVIOUS calendar year (offset -1 on every row), end month 4 in the year `Year` names. Boro is the irrigated dry-season crop, so it is the one Bangladesh season that spans the year boundary.
No date fields on these rows. Months are the standard Bangladeshi Rabi window, and the -1 offset is consistent with Boro, which is derived and sits inside Rabi.
No date fields on these rows. Bangladesh splits Kharif into Kharif-1 (Mar-Jun) and Kharif-2 (Jul-Oct); the source gives only 'Kharif', so this is the span of the two.
Annual aggregate; no single planting or harvest month applies.

Harvest month DERIVED: the source stamps Start and End Period as month 5 on all 1,754 rows. This is the Dong xuan (winter-spring) crop, transplanted Nov-Dec of the previous year, so the planting month and -1 offset are from the published Vietnamese season calendar, not the source.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 5 on all 1,000 rows. Dong xuan; planting from the published calendar.

Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 10 on all 191 rows. RELABELLED - this label covers 1976-1994 only and is continued by 'Northern Autumn Rice' from 1995, with identical stamps and no overlapping keys. See docs/SEASONS.md.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 10 on all 295 rows. RELABELLED - continued by 'Southern Autumn Rice' from 1995.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 10 on all 349 rows. Successor label to 'Northern Summer Rice' from 1995; identical stamp.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 10 on all 540 rows. Successor label to 'Southern Summer Rice' from 1995.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 11 or 12 on all 1,754 rows; 11 taken as the earlier. This is the Mua (main/tenth-month) crop. Planting from the published calendar.
Harvest month DERIVED: source stamps month 12 on all 980 rows. Mua; planting from the published calendar.

Annual aggregate. The source stamps December, which is an end-of-year marker rather than a harvest date. 10 of 10,601 rows (all cassava, 1986-1990, south-central provinces) carry a Start Period year 3 years before or 2 years after `Year` - a defect in the stamp, not in `Year`, and unused here.

NO date fields exist anywhere in the Thai source - Start and End Period are empty on all 32,779 rows. These months are the main rainfed (southwest monsoon) season. Thailand applies 'Wet' across many crops, so this describes a growing regime, not a crop calendar, and whether `year` is the harvest year is UNVERIFIED for Thailand.
No date fields in the source. Months are the second, largely irrigated season. Same caveats as 'Wet'.
Annual or perennial aggregate; no single window applies.

The source leaves Season empty on 15,505 rows, mostly perennials (rubber, oil palm, the tree fruits). 'Unspecified' is a sentinel added by prepare_stats.py because StableBound rejects null seasons; it is not a season.

One row only (VN.ADM1.00019, 1990), and it is the same row as Vietnam's unlabelled `nan` crop. It should disappear when that crop is dropped in packaging; the entry exists so a join cannot silently fail if it survives.
Malaysia's main rice season (musim utama), planted around the start of the northeast monsoon. No date fields in the source.
The off-season (musim luar), largely irrigated. No date fields in the source.
Annual aggregate; no single window applies.
Annual aggregate.

Harvest month DERIVED: the source stamps month 3 on all 43,817 rows. Maha is the northeast-monsoon season, sown around October of the PREVIOUS calendar year - so the planting month and -1 offset come from the published Sri Lankan calendar, not the source, whose planting_year always equals harvest_year and is therefore only a stamp.
Harvest month DERIVED: the source stamps month 8 on all 36,779 rows. Yala is the southwest-monsoon season, sown around May, within the same calendar year. Planting month from the published calendar.
Annual aggregate; the source stamps December, an end-of-year marker.
Annual aggregate spanning both seasons; the source stamps August.
Japan's main rice season. The source carries NO planting or harvest dates on any of its 129,618 rows, so these months are from the published Japanese calendar.

No date fields in the source. A winter crop sown late in the year is harvested in the following one, hence the +1 harvest offset - UNVERIFIED against the source, which gives no dates.
No date fields in the source. Same caveat as Winter.
Annual aggregate - and Japan's largest season label by far (67,570 of its rows).

The source carries a single season label for every Indonesian row, including rice, which is in practice grown in two main plantings - a wet-season crop harvested around Feb-Apr and a dry-season crop around Jul-Sep. The source does not separate them, so no single planting or harvest month applies. year is the calendar year of the annual total.
Annual aggregate. The source has no date fields; Start and End Period are empty on every row. Most Korean crops carry this label.
Spring plantings (spring potato, spring Napa cabbage and radish, spring onion), sown around March-April and harvested around June-July. No date fields in the source.
Fall plantings (fall potato, fall Napa cabbage and radish), sown around August-September and harvested around October-November. No date fields in the source.

Winter Napa cabbage and radish, mostly Jeju, sown in autumn and harvested over the winter. The +1 harvest offset assumes year is the sowing year, which is UNVERIFIED - the source gives no dates. Only 46 rows.
